system_description.narrative_title: Maritime escalation in the Middle East threatens global oil and shipping
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid escalation of attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure around the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea — driven by Iran-aligned forces (including the Houthis) and entangled regional states — is disrupting oil flows, raising prices and forcing operational and military adjustments. Diplomatic efforts (Gulf talks, BRICS calls for restraint) and great-power manoeuvres (US naval posture, limits on tanker defence windows, China/India engagement) are simultaneously trying to contain contagion, creating feedbacks between security, markets and diplomacy. The situation is an open system: tactical attacks and infrastructure outages feed market reactions and alliance choices, which in turn alter incentives for further escalation or restraint.
system_description.scope: Inside: maritime chokepoints and routes (Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Red Sea), oil export infrastructure (Saudi East-West pipeline, ports, tankers), state and non-state military actors (Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Houthis, Iraqi militias, US and allied naval forces), operational responses (air-defence time slots, rerouting, insurance), market variables (oil supply, prices, risk premium), and diplomatic processes (Gulf-Iran talks, BRICS mediation). This system contains both abstract systemic variables (supply shocks, risk perception, escalation dynamics, diplomatic leverage) and concrete entities/events (pipelines, seized islands, specific state actors and naval deployments).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economy: the intersection of international security, global energy markets and great-power competition (US, China, Russia and the expanding BRICS).
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil & energy markets (production, inventories, pricing, traders)
International shipping and logistics (routes, insurance, commercial operators)
Great-power strategic competition and diplomacy (US-China-Russia, BRICS influence)
Regional security architectures and state politics (Gulf states, Iran, Yemen conflict dynamics)
evidence_headlines: Saudi Arabia shuts East-West pipeline that bypasses Hormuz after attacks
New Strait of Hormuz ship attack raises oil supply fears as Iran war widens
Houthis seize Red Sea islands in lightning offensive
Iran says Hormuz reopening depends on U.S. meeting its conditions
BRICS adopts joint declaration, urges 'maximum restraint' in Mideast
US limits air defence time slots for tankers sailing through Hormuz

variables.name: Maritime attack frequency
variables.description: The rate at which hostile incidents (attacks, strikes, interdictions) occur against commercial ships and maritime infrastructure in the region.

variables.name: Non-state offensive capability
variables.description: The aggregate kinetic and logistical capability of irregular or proxy forces to carry out maritime or energy-infrastructure attacks.

variables.name: Naval/military presence level
variables.description: The aggregate deployed military assets, patrol intensity and readiness in maritime areas affecting commercial transit.

variables.name: Protective window duration
variables.description: Average length of time per transit that commercial vessels receive active defensive coverage or escort protection.

variables.name: Shipping rerouting burden
variables.description: Average additional distance, time and operational burden imposed on commercial shipping due to avoidance of high-risk routes.

variables.name: Chokepoint transit volume
variables.description: Volume of commercial maritime traffic transiting critical maritime chokepoints per unit time.

variables.name: Infrastructure outage rate
variables.description: Frequency and duration-weighted rate of outages and service interruptions across oil export pipelines, terminals and related facilities.

variables.name: Oil export flow
variables.description: Volume of crude oil and refined product exports moving through regional routes and facilities per unit time.

variables.name: Oil export capacity
variables.description: Maximum technically available throughput of export infrastructure (pipelines, terminals, tanker availability) absent operational disruptions.

variables.name: Market risk premium
variables.description: Incremental price component embedded in oil and shipping markets that reflects perceived geopolitical and conflict risk.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: prevailing market price level for benchmark crude oil relevant to global trade and regional export economics.

variables.name: Insurance and security premium
variables.description: Average insurance, armed-guard and security surcharge applied to vessels and cargo operating in the affected maritime zone.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: Short-term variability and uncertainty in commodity, freight and financial markets driven by the maritime-security situation.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: Frequency, scale and depth of diplomatic interactions, negotiations and mediation efforts aimed at conflict containment or resolution.

variables.name: Diplomatic leverage balance
variables.description: Net capacity of diplomatic incentives, sanctions and bargaining power to influence actors' choices toward escalation or restraint.

variables.name: Great-power competition intensity
variables.description: Degree of strategic rivalry and external-state involvement that shapes incentives, support networks and constraints in the regional system.

catalysts.title: Iran–Gulf talks on Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Planned negotiations between Iran and Gulf states to reach an agreement on Hormuz navigation and security, potentially altering transit rules and escorts.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran and Gulf states to meet in push for Hormuz deal'; 'No signed Hormuz deal expected yet'; Oman meeting postponed.

catalysts.title: Houthi consolidation in Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb
catalysts.description: Houthis solidify control of Red Sea islands and approaches to Bab el‑Mandeb, enabling sustained interdiction of shipping and chokepoint disruption.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthis seize Red Sea islands'; 'Houthis take effective control of key Red Sea chokepoint'; 'Houthis reach Dhubab'.

catalysts.title: East–West pipeline outage and repair process
catalysts.description: Damage to Saudi East–West pipeline forces prolonged shutdown and repair decisions, threatening near-term export capacity and flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi Arabia shuts East-West pipeline'; 'Satellite images show extent of damage'; 'pipeline outage threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply.'

catalysts.title: US limits air-defense time slots for tankers
catalysts.description: US policy reducing scheduled air-defense coverage windows for tankers transiting Hormuz, changing protective arrangements for commercial shipping.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US limits air defence time slots for tankers sailing through Hormuz' — immediate policy reducing coverage.

catalysts.title: Demining mission in Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Planned or ongoing mine-clearance operations in the Strait of Hormuz to restore safe transit lanes and reduce explosive hazards to shipping.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'The risky mission to de-mine the Strait of Hormuz' — demining likely to be undertaken near term.

catalysts.title: Follow‑up militia/proxy strikes on oil infrastructure
catalysts.description: Further drone/strike operations by militias or proxies targeting pipelines and terminals, prolonging outages and export disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi pipeline attack exposes potent Iraqi militia threat'; 'drone attacks against Saudi Arabia' signal risk of follow-ups.

catalysts.title: BRICS diplomatic push for Gulf restraint
catalysts.description: BRICS leaders and finance ministers press for restraint and mediation in the Gulf, potentially catalysing alternate diplomatic channels.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Brics push for Gulf peace'; 'BRICS adopts joint declaration, urges maximum restraint'; Xi urges BRICS peace role.

catalysts.title: US ambassador nomination to Saudi Arabia
catalysts.description: US nomination of a new ambassador to Riyadh (confirmation process) could affect bilateral diplomatic channels and military coordination.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump nominates Republican lawmaker as ambassador to Saudi Arabia' — nomination may change bilateral engagement.
